title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

reading.body:
This is an access-control failure inside a law enforcement deployment. A licensed user of the Flock camera system and of state databases, CJIS and CORI, is accused of running location queries for a personal purpose rather than a policing one. The systems performed as designed: they returned location data to someone holding valid credentials. Nothing in the reporting indicates the queries were blocked, flagged, or reviewed at the time they were made.

The failure sits at the point where a legitimate account meets an illegitimate purpose. Flock and the state databases are built to serve officers conducting investigations, and the controls that exist are credential checks, not purpose checks. Catching this would have required auditing query logs against case numbers or authorisations, or a review triggered by repeated searches for one person over two years. The reporting does not say whether any such audit existed or fired.

The internal affairs investigation took four weeks and concluded the systems were misused, and a criminal complaint was filed. That is an administrative finding and a charging decision, not a conviction. Whether Rogers acted as alleged, and whether any oversight mechanism failed or simply was not present, is not established by the reporting.

reports.title: Stow police officer accused of misusing Flock system to track former partner

summary:
A Stow police officer, Jason Rogers, is accused of using police databases to track a woman he previously dated. The woman said she ended the relationship about five years ago, changed her identity, phone number, and social media habits after leaving. She discovered this summer that Rogers had searched for her location through the Flock camera system and other law enforcement databases, including CJIS and CORI, multiple times in 2024 and 2025. She also said he drove by her home.

The Stow Police Department filed a criminal complaint against Rogers on July 17 and found after a four-week internal affairs investigation that he misused state systems. He was placed on paid leave in July, then unpaid leave as of July 31. The woman has a restraining order against him lasting at least a year. A Select Board hearing is scheduled next week, when town leaders could vote on Rogers' employment status.
